activities.description: Varsity Track & Field (Pole Vaulter) Varsity Rock Climbing (Captain) National Honor Society (President) Teen Court (Leadership Board Member) I essentially judge real youth criminal cases instead of an adult judge.

activities.name: 3 Star Space Force General: 11/10 literally the best letter I could have ever as
activities.description: 3 Star Space Force General: 11/10 literally the best letter I could have ever asked for from the best person I could ever ask for. The general had been a family friend and knew me since birth, they were able to masterfully articulate my interests into the Air Force lingo, and speak (almost two pages) on their personal relationship with me. Literally the Greatest Of All Time.

activities.name: 1 Star Air Force General: 8.5/10 it was short, and this general and I didn’t hav
activities.description: 1 Star Air Force General: 8.5/10 it was short, and this general and I didn’t have a super big connection before my parents introduced me to him and he offered to write me a rec letter, our relationship has strengthened lengths after he ended up writing a letter though. He called me a unicorn candidate, and said if he had to build up the military again from day 1, I would be his first choice to lead that, so overall W letter.

activities.name: Math Teacher 7.5/10 really spoke well about my desire to serve my country and ho
activities.description: Math Teacher 7.5/10 really spoke well about my desire to serve my country and how well I performed in his class, which math had been a struggle on my resume since I got a C in Algebra II sophomore year.

activities.name: USAFA interview: 5.5/10 It was my only one conducted over video instead of in pe
activities.description: USAFA interview: 5.5/10 It was my only one conducted over video instead of in person, the dude had a name I couldn’t hope to pronounce correctly, and generally I didn’t “vibe” with as much as my other interviewers. I completed it fine but it was definitely my worst overall, I went off track multiple times and didn’t hone my answers very well. I majorly messed up here and it almost probably cost me my dream school, but oh well.

activities.name: West Point Interview: 8.5/10 My interviewer was a great guy, and still checks in
activities.description: West Point Interview: 8.5/10 My interviewer was a great guy, and still checks in to see how I’m doing. He really helped me out a lot, in addition to asking the questions I had the best answers for. He also bought me garlic fries because a school shooting happened that day a little north of my school and I knew some friends from Boys State who went there.

activities.name: House of Representatives interview: 7/10, interview is mediocre, not because I d
activities.description: House of Representatives interview: 7/10, interview is mediocre, not because I did poorly (I did great!), but because the interviewer’s (3 people) were all “bros bros” and high key said some weird stuff about women serving in the military. My mom is a disabled veteran who served 28 years, so this is a big no-no for me personally, and not a good way of thought for the rest of the military but other than that it was alright. On the plus side one of the interviewers was a politician I had been wanting to meet for about a year, and I just happened to have him on my interview panel.

activities.name: United States Senate Interview: 7/10, this one was actually meh, I was able to g
activities.description: United States Senate Interview: 7/10, this one was actually meh, I was able to go to my best stories, but I went off track a noticeable amount of times, and my interviewers were all West Pointers, and were dogging on me because the Air Force / Army football game was coming up (in a joking way). I like the people on the panel and I liked the interview overall, it’s just not as good as some of my others, but not as bad as my Air Force one.

activities.name: Every school got a very deeply personal essay on how in Teen Court, I came acros
activities.description: Every school got a very deeply personal essay on how in Teen Court, I came across my friend who had stole alcohol, and because the panel was only 3 people, I had to stay on and judge his case, and give him a sentence. (Made sure to subtly include the academies honor codes/concept… I will not lie, cheat, steal… in a way that was +aura to the admissions people) I chose the hard sentence we had after wrestling with my conscience for a hot hour there, and months later, he told me how much it meant to give back, and now we serve on Teen Court together. All academies had different essays after this, but most of the could be piled into the “I want to serve because I saw it in my family and want to make my own path, I want to challenge myself and lead America’s sons and daughters, and I want to repay the debt I owe my country” pile.
